claims.title: Daniel 7 uses beast imagery for kingdoms
claims.assessment: The passage explicitly interprets the beasts as kingdoms/kings; identification of the fourth as Seleucid vs Roman varies by interpretive tradition.

claims.title: Antiochus IV enforced conformity and suppressed Jewish worship
claims.assessment: 1 Maccabees 1:41–61 describes decrees, forced sacrifices, prohibitions and punishment. It does not establish an ancient universal marketplace-token requirement or 'first ever' boycott.

claims.title: Ancient Israel's God is identical to Satan
claims.assessment: Isaiah 45:7 and Job 1–2 are pertinent primary texts; they do not, on their own, prove God and Satan are one identical being. Preserve as the source author's theological interpretation, not settled philology.

claims.title: Quirinius conducted a census of Judea in 6/7 CE
claims.assessment: Josephus reports a Roman assessment in Judea and Judas's opposition. This cannot simply be identified without qualification with Luke 2: the chronology is disputed.

claims.title: Judas the Galilean opposed Roman tax assessment and claimed God alone as ruler
claims.assessment: Directly described by Josephus. Josephus also attributes later violent unrest to the movement; avoid characterizing it as only peaceful or digital disconnection.

claims.title: Papyrus 115 preserves the 616 reading
claims.assessment: P.Oxy. 4499 preserves 616. The widespread reading 666 is also ancient, and 616 was already known to Irenaeus before this papyrus was written. P115 is not proof that every original exemplar read 616.

claims.title: 666 and 616 can encode forms of Nero Caesar
claims.assessment: A prominent, well-supported gematria proposal: Hebrew transliteration of Neron Caesar -> 666; omitting final nun -> 616. Not mathematically exclusive proof that every Revelation image refers only to Nero.

claims.title: Charagma means mark or stamp
claims.assessment: Greek lexical meaning is supported; alleged obligatory incense-and-token processing before every Roman market purchase is not demonstrated by the lexical evidence.

claims.title: Romans universally required imperial incense/token for market purchases
claims.assessment: No evidence found in the consulted primary/lexical sources for a universal rule that every Roman merchant had to sacrifice at an altar and receive a trade token. Do not assert as fact.

claims.title: Atomic design systems use tokens, components, and interfaces
claims.assessment: A valid technical architecture analogy. UI design tokens, pixels and diodes are distinct physical/software concepts, not literal subatomic identity markers.

claims.title: Digital services can mediate access to finances and identity
claims.assessment: Assess by concrete product, jurisdiction, user group and fallback methods; universal claims that cash and offline transactions cannot occur are incorrect.

claims.title: Every individual is already marked by a global AI matrix
claims.assessment: The source's theological-metaphorical conclusion is not an empirically established universal fact. Do not equate ordinary phone use or digital payments with compulsory worship.

claims.title: In God We Trust on US money proves religious compliance system
claims.assessment: Presence of the national motto on currency and the theological claim that it is the mark are separate propositions. The latter is interpretation.

sources.title: Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews, Book XVIII, chapter 1
